register.name: Distribution Connected Accelerator Program, with Infradebt
register.detail: Clean Energy Finance Corporation · announced 3 August 2026 · up to 16 hybrid solar, battery and battery retrofit projects of up to 5MW
register.note: Mid-scale projects connected to the distribution network, the “missing middle” of the energy transition
register.text: A CEFC commitment of A$100 million to a programme with Infradebt, an infrastructure debt fund manager, to develop up to 16 hybrid solar, battery and battery retrofit projects. It finances distribution-connected assets of up to 5MW and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Green Treasury Bond due June 2036
register.detail: AOFM · coupon 5.00% · matures 21 June 2036 · syndicated May 2026, settled 26 May 2026 · yield 5.065%
register.note: A$24.4 billion of bids at the final clearing price
register.text: A Green Treasury Bond of the Commonwealth of Australia, issued by syndication in May 2026. The Commonwealth allocates an amount equal to its net proceeds to eligible green expenditures under three goals: climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation and improved environmental outcomes.

register.name: Treasury Bond issuance, 2026-27
register.detail: Australian Office of Financial Management · Budget 2026-27, 13 May 2026 · update of 26 June 2026
register.note: About A$79 billion to refinance maturing bonds and about A$46 billion of net issuance
register.text: Treasury Bonds, including Green Treasury Bonds, planned for 2026-27. The plan adds new bonds maturing in 2038 and 2057 by syndication, and a first Treasury bond referencing monthly inflation in the second half of 2026-27.

register.name: Housing Australia Future Fund Facility and National Housing Accord Facility, Rounds One and Two
register.detail: Housing Australia · 279 projects · 9,284 social and 9,366 affordable homes · rounds completed 30 June 2025 · Round Three opened January 2026
register.note: Round One A$10,230 million and Round Two A$3,791 million
register.text: Availability payments, concessional loans and grants from Housing Australia, with contracts signed, that support a pipeline of more than 18,650 social and affordable homes across Australia. It serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Household Energy Upgrades Fund
register.detail: Clean Energy Finance Corporation · A$1 billion fund · lenders include Brighte, Commonwealth Bank, ING, Plenti, Plico and Westpac
register.note: Committed by the CEFC through the fund, supporting more than A$1 billion of discounted household lending (11 August 2026)
register.text: Low-interest loans through banks and lenders for solar panels, batteries, heat pumps, insulation and other upgrades to existing homes. CSIRO analysis of fund data finds that households save an average of A$1,700 to A$2,300 a year on electricity bills, which serves the energy standard at home.

register.name: National Agreement on Social Housing and Homelessness
register.detail: Australian Government with the states and territories · five years from 1 July 2024 · announced 26 June 2024
register.note: Doubles Commonwealth funding for homelessness, which the states and territories must match
register.text: Commonwealth funding shared by the states and territories over five years for social housing and homelessness services. It serves the shelter standard for people without a secure home.

register.name: Green Treasury Bond due June 2034 (inaugural)
register.detail: AOFM · coupon 4.25% · matures 21 June 2034 · priced 4 June 2024 · yield 4.295%
register.note: Final order book of A$22.89 billion, more than three times the size; 91 unique investors
register.text: The first Green Treasury Bond of the Commonwealth of Australia, sold by syndication in June 2024. Its proceeds are matched to eligible green expenditures, with annual allocation and impact reports from the AOFM from 2025.

register.name: Remote housing in the Northern Territory
register.detail: Australian and Northern Territory Governments · announced 12 March 2024 · up to 2,700 new homes by mid-2034 · 300 built by 12 January 2026
register.note: A joint investment over 10 years; a separate A$120 million Commonwealth contribution over three years for homelands
register.text: A joint investment of the Australian and Northern Territory Governments in new homes for remote First Nations communities and town camps. It serves the shelter standard and the national commitment to Close the Gap.

register.name: Sustainability bond, 15 years
register.detail: Housing Australia · Affordable Housing Bond Aggregator · issued 8 November 2023 · 15-year tenor · AAA-rated, Government-guaranteed
register.note: Housing Australia has issued over A$2.8 billion of social and sustainability bonds since March 2019
register.text: A bond whose net proceeds are used to provide loans to registered community housing providers. At issue, Housing Australia announced its largest lending deal, A$517 million to the Building Communities consortium for 1,370 new homes in Melbourne, of which up to A$422 million through the bond aggregator; it serves the shelter standard.

items.text: Grazing and grain across almost half the continent.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: A continent of sun and wind, with room for the energy of a region.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: A quarter of the power renewable in 2021, and rising fast with sun and wind.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 17.7% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: OzHarvest
items.text: A food rescue organisation that collects surplus food and delivers it to charities: 35,096,144 meals and 1,544 charities supported in 2025, with hampers now reaching remote communities such as Jabiru in the Northern Territory. Income from its catering, Refettorio and OzHarvest Ventures products supports the work.

items.name: SecondBite
items.text: One of Australia’s largest food relief organisations, which rescues surplus food from growers, manufacturers and retailers for charities and community groups. Since its merger with FareShare on 1 July 2024 it also cooks rescued food into ready-to-eat meals: more than 2.8 million in the first year.

items.name: Purple House
items.text: An Indigenous owned and operated health service that has brought people with kidney failure home to Country for dialysis for more than 20 years, across 20 remote communities in the Northern Territory, Western Australia and South Australia, with more than 11,000 treatments a year. It also runs Bush Balm, a bush medicine social enterprise.

items.name: Nightingale Housing
items.text: A not-for-profit that delivers homes sold to residents and community housing providers, not investors, at prices set to recover the costs of funding, land, design and building.

items.name: Pingala
items.text: A community energy organisation helping renters and people living in apartments and social housing to access renewable energy. In March 2026 it launched the Goulburn Community Solar Farm, which it describes as the first community-owned solar and battery farm in New South Wales, expected to power about 500 homes.

items.name: Vanguard Laundry
items.text: A work-integrated social enterprise laundry, established in Toowoomba, Queensland, in 2016, that employs people facing complex barriers to work in a commercial laundry for hospitals, motels and mining camps. It creates around seventy new employment opportunities each year, and about thirty staff move into long-term employment in the open market each year.
